blocks.content: Seismic waves are generated by earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. Their speed and direction change depending on the material they pass through.
Important: S-waves cannot pass through liquids. Their absence beyond a certain depth proves that the outer core is liquid.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Seismic waves are energy waves caused by the sudden breaking of rock within the earth or an explosion.
Shadow zones are specific areas on the Earth's surface where seismographs cannot detect direct seismic waves.
The existence and extent of shadow zones provide direct evidence regarding the physical state and density of Earth's interior layers.
Focus on the exact angular distance ranges for P-wave and S-wave shadow zones.
Remember that S-waves cannot travel through liquids, which defines the boundaries of the Earth's outer core shadow zone.

blocks.content:
P-wave shadow zone: 103°–142° from the epicenter.

S-wave shadow zone: Beyond 103° due to liquid outer core.
